claims.text: A multi-fidelity surrogate combining limited DFT/MD simulations with experimentally informed machine learning can rapidly and accurately predict Young’s modulus, yield strength, and toughness for hierarchical-heterostructured HfNbTiVAl10.
The reported HfNbTiVAl10 state is a hierarchical heterostructure featuring multilevel chemical fluctuations.
High-fidelity simulations of representative microstructural domains can generate physically informative training data for a lower-cost surrogate.
The surrogate should be evaluated under controlled room-temperature tensile and fracture conditions with realistic strain rates.
The training data should span the microstructural variations present in the reported hierarchical state.
Multilevel chemical fluctuations and associated local lattice distortions are characteristic of hierarchical-heterostructured HfNbTiVAl10.
These chemical fluctuations and lattice distortions mediate the relationship between microstructure and macroscopic mechanical properties.
High-fidelity outputs concerning local distortions and phase stability can capture essential alloy physics.
A machine-learning model can interpolate high-fidelity results across the full compositional and microstructural variability of hierarchical HfNbTiVAl10.
The data-fidelity hierarchy efficiently encodes elastic, plastic, and fracture-related microstructural rearrangements into a rapid predictor.
The proposed framework could reduce prediction errors by approximately 30% relative to standalone CALPHAD or first-principles methods.
The proposed framework could be approximately one order of magnitude faster than conventional high-throughput calculations.
Extensive CALPHAD and related high-throughput calculations impose meaningful computational-efficiency constraints in HEA discovery.
Prior high-demand machine-learning approaches lack explicit microstructural mediation.
Unseen nonlinear phase transitions can make the surrogate unreliable.
Unrepresented defect mechanisms or microstructural variation outside the training domain can make the surrogate unreliable.
Descriptors that fail to represent interactions among local chemical fluctuations can degrade predictive accuracy.
The quantitative gains depend on the quality and representativeness of the high-fidelity data and on descriptor selection.
A blinded prospective benchmark would record predictions before independent tensile, fracture, and microstructural testing of replicated HfNbTiVAl10 samples.
The hypothesis is falsified if more than 30% of measured properties fall outside predicted 95% confidence intervals or if systematic deviations exceed the specified baseline-relative error criterion.
